runs.caption: The hotspot sits on the head capsule and the mandible bases - exactly the region a key uses to separate the trap-jaw genera.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Diffuse and mostly background. P(Anochetus) is only 0.04 on this photo and rises mainly when the Odontomachus mesosoma is hidden (deep blue), not when any one region is revealed.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Again the head and mandible-base region carries the decision; the gaster contributes little.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Odontomachus evidence on this Anochetus also concentrates at the head end, matching the 2018 comparison, though the hot region spills onto the background left of the head.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Attention spreads over the whole mid-body rather than any single character - plausible for a genus told by overall habitus, but the least localised map of the true-genus set.
runs.creator: Nick Olgeirson

runs.caption: The gaster is the hottest region, with a secondary spot toward the head - plausibly the gastral segmentation that separates Technomyrmex from Tapinoma.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Tapinoma evidence on the same photograph comes from the head region instead: the two look-alike dolichoderines are read from different body parts.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: One clean hotspot on the head and the front of the mesosoma.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: Head and gaster light up - the same gaster signal as on the true Technomyrmex above - but one blob at bottom right sits on plain background.
runs.creator: April Nobile

runs.caption: An honest surprise: the map favours the head capsule and the gaster, not the famous trap jaws - the long mandibles alone are apparently not what the embedding keys on.
runs.creator: April Nobile
